result.rationale:
TopicEmbed.import unescaped-interpolates the feed-supplied url into the HTML footer: `contents << "\n
\n...#{url}..."`, and the only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. Since single quotes are valid URI characters, an attacker-controlled feed/link like `http://x/'onfocus='alert(1)` passes the scheme check and injects attributes/markup into post raw HTML, which is cooked verbatim due to cook_method raw_html (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). This is a real XSS vector introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb, TopicEmbed.import appends HTML containing an #{url} constructed via string interpolation after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. Apostrophes are valid in URLs, so a crafted URL containing `'` can break out of the single-quoted href attribute and inject additional attributes/HTML. This is especially dangerous here because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (see Post#cook returning `raw`), and embed/best.html.erb renders `raw post.cooked`, so the injected HTML/attributes would be output unsanitized.
